done_when: When forge merge enable finds its earlier fix whose only change is forge.toml's merge setting and the default branch has moved on, it rebuilds that change on the current default branch (same fix, the default branch's forge.toml with only merge set to agent) instead of merging, so no conflict appears; it still never merges the change itself; a command test covers a repo adopted on an earlier release that upgraded after an interrupted merge enable

findings.body: The shared filter accepts every changed line beginning with `merge =`, even inside a TOML multiline string. A valid multiline `test` command containing a Python assignment such as `merge = [...]` can therefore be edited locally or in another checkout and still pass both the local check and remote-history validation. Multiline command strings are supported by `src/forge/repo.py:311` and its TOML parser at line 390. When the default advances, reset at line 189 discards the local command edit; force-publication at line 199 overwrites the remote edit because its tip was incorrectly classified as safe. This violates the rule that "data is protected against loss." Validate that changes affect the actual top-level merge setting, including each remote revision, and add a command regression covering an unrelated edit inside a multiline setting.
findings.title: Standard: Data is protected against loss

why: forge merge enable resumes a fix branch made before the repo upgraded Forge (its forge.toml still pins the old release plus merge = agent), so merging the default branch always conflicts on forge.toml's version line (reported by a client session after upgrading to v1.2.7)
